observations.statement: The three references rank static < pooled < target-aware DIN-style in full validation AUC (0.6050036144838207, 0.6102261137080656, 0.6133619861190683); both history additions lower Logloss. This establishes useful history information locally, not a particular semantic bottleneck.

All 34 allowed trial receipts report success with null errors; previous_runtime_error is null. Negative performance is distinct from execution failure. No additional failed or abandoned execution is invented.

Full behavior-count correction loses AUC and worsens Logloss for both pooling and DIN. Half correction improves pooling, but DIN still trails ordinary and full correction on AUC. The weaker-strength follow-up was informative and unsuccessful for DIN; count correction and product-gradient scaling are distinct interventions.

The round-3 aligned product restriction gains 0.001162954694291618 AUC over the ordinary adapter; removing cross products alone nearly recovers the gain. Removing context products alone improves AUC but worsens loss. Single removals interact subadditively on AUC. Same-seed replay/inline bridges preserve metrics but do not explain the ordinary-adapter versus original-DIN offset.

Aligned unit products beat aligned raw by 0.0004876567525730069 AUC and lower Logloss. The crossed replacement obtains almost no AUC gain from normalization and worsens loss. Alignment remains favored with unit norms and with detached denominator gradients. Scalar product magnitude alone is not an adequate account, conditional on implementation isolation; semantic causality remains unestablished.

Backward controls have identical reported same-state forward values but different trained outcomes. Projection helps AUC at unscaled, event inverse-norm and fixed 0.2 scales, with different magnitudes. Fixed scaling nearly matches full-rule AUC; the earlier interpretation that exact event-adaptive scaling is necessary is weakened. Full remains lower in Logloss.

Round-9 full and fixed replays exactly reproduce prior AUC, Logloss and 23 slices. Whole-history reassignment loses AUC and loss versus full. Whole-history mean gives AUC 0.6149872680212398, numerically near fixed/full but with worse loss; no equivalence or independent repetition follows.

Latest action mean: AUC 0.614672318575737, Logloss 0.19661644463258673. Relative to full, AUC falls 0.0003093726040777067 and loss rises 0.0000530370412560599. It also trails whole-history mean on both metrics. This is negative evidence for this action-conditioned averaging implementation.

Latest within-action reassignment: AUC 0.6147849008671875, Logloss 0.19668868647099816. Relative to full, AUC falls 0.00019679031262720414 and loss rises 0.0001252788796674842. Compared with whole-history reassignment, AUC improves 0.00005506760961559998 while loss worsens 0.00010368999373616683; AUC-only partial recovery is not a general rescue.

The mean-minus-reassignment AUC contrast changes from +0.0002574347636679075 across whole histories to -0.00011258229145050258 within action groups. Grouping-by-operation AUC difference in differences is -0.0003700170551184101; corresponding Logloss contrast is -0.0000927367050647665. Mean has lower loss than reassignment in both groupings. The interaction is descriptive at seed 42, not a semantic decomposition.

Neither latest arm improves the incumbent: action mean/fixed AUC delta -0.00031652696608786; action reassigned/fixed -0.00020394467463735744, both with worse loss. Both still exceed original DIN at this seed; inherited architecture gains cannot be attributed to the new grouping intervention.

Each latest arm loses AUC in 21 of 23 overlapping slices versus full and has worse Logloss in all 23. Action mean improves AUC only in history lengths 1-16 and 17-64; action reassignment only in lengths 17-64 and hour 6-12. These slice counts are exploratory, not independent statistical votes.

Latest diagnostics report 512 ordered validation impressions, 60475 regular events, 4 empty histories, no natural floor/boundary cases, and action-code event counts 57171/1634/650/1020. Own/action reassigned correlation is about -0.103; the reassignment changes about 96.15% of eligible scales. Group sums and reassigned squared sums are preserved in sampled states to roughly 2.1e-7 relative error. Moment preservation does not preserve gradient norms or optimizer updates.

Latest candidate diagnostics report zero same-state full/active forward product and logit differences; zero padding mass and empty summaries. Synthetic VJP audits now report errors at most 3.602e-15 across six modes, with one boundary and four floored synthetic events and only two probes per mode. Submission notes said these measurements were unknown at submission; committed diagnostic results now exist. These remain candidate-supplied bounded checks, not an independent audit of training updates.

Latest arms and closest history controls all have 17130275 parameters (17078688 embeddings, 51587 dense). Action mean/reassignment wall time is 620.45/622.35 seconds, train time 529.88/532.86 seconds, peak memory approximately 835.10 MB. Latest faster inference measurements relative to round 9 do not establish efficiency: recipes are matched, but round-specific gathering, scheduling and diagnostics can vary.

interpretations.statement: Behavior-stratified scale preservation did not remove the reassignment penalty. The narrow explanation that the entire whole-history reassignment penalty is caused by transporting scales across action types is weakened by this implementation.
interpretations.qualification: Conditional on per-history/action grouping and inherited forward/backward isolation described in receipts. One deterministic reassignment, seed 42 only; within-action time/order/direction correlations remain.

interpretations.statement: Grouping and scale operation interact on observed ranking. Action-conditioned averaging underperforms whole-history averaging, while restricting reassignment gives a small AUC recovery and worsens loss. A general claim that finer action-specific allocation helps is unsupported.
interpretations.qualification: Controlled local performance contrast conditional on source isolation; not repeated support or identified causal mechanism.

interpretations.statement: Moderate shared scaling remains a plausible optimizer-conditioning explanation. Near-best AUC from full, fixed and whole-history mean does not imply identical mechanisms or performance equivalence. Action mean failure weakens the stronger assertion that any averaging replacement suffices.

Preserved action-wise scale moments plus nonzero reassignment activity narrow a scalar-marginal explanation, but do not identify semantic relevance. Norm-direction association, temporal order, cross-action update coupling and Adam moments remain possible mediators.

Constant tangent remains the numerical AUC incumbent. Its approximately 7.15e-6 AUC advantage over full is preliminary; full has lower Logloss. No practical superiority, significance, calibration diagnosis, robustness, external novelty or final-assessment success is established.

alternatives.explanation: Action grouping changes within-group variance, singleton handling and scale-to-time/direction correlations. The deterministic permutation is mildly anticorrelated with own scales, not independent random destruction of semantic information.

alternatives.explanation: Preserving sum and squared sum of scales does not preserve the norm or direction of summed embedding gradients, per-parameter Adam moments, clipping, or update energy. Mean replacement additionally removes variation.
alternatives.discriminating_check: Use fixed-state independent VJP probes and, only if an authorized later interface supplies it, a bounded gradient/update diagnostic at matched states. Do not call scalar moment matching equal effective compute or equal learning rate.

alternatives.explanation: Shared embedding adaptation changes group means, query norms and empty-history predictions. Cross-checkpoint diagnostic differences are consequences of training and cannot mediate performance causally.
alternatives.discriminating_check: Keep training and forward data fixed; interpret fixed-state diagnostics as implementation/activity checks, not relevance measures. Include empty-history and rare-positive loss costs.

falsifiers.current_status: Supported by bounded candidate-reported same-state forward and synthetic VJP checks, not independently verified.

falsifiers.current_status: Unverified, selected seed-42 AUC gap approximately 7.15e-6 and loss tradeoff.
falsifiers.future_falsifying_evidence: Nonpositive mean paired AUC delta or unstable signs weakens superiority. No switch to loss as primary after seeing results.

limitations: All 34 trials use seed 42; deterministic bridge equality is not independent repetition. No standard errors, equivalence margins, p-values or significance inferred from aggregate metrics.
Adaptive reuse of validation may inflate selected gains. Additional seeds test initialization robustness but do not remove selection bias. No test/withheld feedback is authorized or accessed.

No raw data, actual candidate sources, checkpoints, prediction vectors or user-cluster IDs are exported. Host causal/scorer gates and recipe are inherited, not independently rerun. Hashes identify receipts and declared artifacts; they do not verify unseen code or checkpoints.

One deterministic reassignment rule with about -0.103 own/assigned correlation in action groups. Preserving action membership and sampled scalar moments does not isolate semantic relevance, causal mediation, update norm or optimizer state.

Grouping changes the support, variance and singleton behavior of scales. Whole-history/action factorial identifies a composite implementation contrast, not a pure action-semantic effect. Older projection factors are not independently varied in latest arms.

Candidate-authored diagnostics cover the ordered first 512 checkpoint impressions, dominated by one action code (57171 of 60475 events). Natural floor/boundary cases are absent; synthetic VJP tests have only two probes/mode and do not validate every training step.

All slice results are exploratory and overlap. Empty histories have 310 positives, pv-absent 397 and frequency-1-2 1045; no sufficiency threshold or subgroup significance is invented. Missing/unseen-field slices are not exported, and histories are truncated at 128 visible events.

Empty-history predictions can change through shared training even when empty summary is zero. AUC/Logloss disagreement does not by itself establish calibration failure or prove semantic attention quality.
Publisher static user/ad snapshot as-of dates are undocumented. The benchmark assumption does not establish production point-in-time availability.

All runs succeeded operationally. Submission-time notes saying untrained or diagnostic outcomes unknown are historical notes; the committed success status and current measurements govern execution status. Tool truncation or unavailable rg is not a scientific failure.

Measured wall/train/memory/batched latency are descriptive; no allocated GPU-time, exact examples-processed metric, repeated timing or measured equal-compute frontier is available. Batch latency includes gathering at batch size 4096, not per-request latency.

Nearest external normalization/surrogate-gradient implementation and priority remain unverified. DIN is a local masked-softmax adaptation, not a full published-model reproduction. DMR full paper was not accessible in the registry; its author README is a field reference only.

Latest knowledge usage has missing prospective assessments for both retrieved industry cards. Their relevance can be assessed now, but adoption, causal knowledge value or an execution link cannot be inferred or retroactively certified.

Only analysis.json is writable. No independent memory writer, model/training/assessment command or formal output schema is exported. Memory updates below are append-only proposals for host ingestion; full model reproduction requires the later authorized interface.
